Simulation.Name: FreshFizz Pricing Challenge
Simulation.Briefing: Marketing: Pricing. Set a selling price in a finite beverage market. Initial price: 2.50 EUR; unit cost: 1.20 EUR; historical share: 18%; market demand: 10,000 units.
Simulation.Objective: Compare the consequences of your decisions with the weighted scoring targets.
Simulation.Theory: A price cut raises relative demand, but profit rises only when extra sales cover the lower contribution margin. Advertising has diminishing returns.
Simulation.Strategy: Compare units sold, margin and inventory after small price changes. Limit marketing to spending that creates additional contribution.

Events.Name: Competitor price cut
Events.Description: The reference competitor lowers its price by 10 percent.

Events.Name: Equilibrium returns
Events.Description: Demand and competitor prices return toward their initial values.

Simulation.Name: Expected Value Decision Lab
Simulation.Briefing: Expected Value: make a decision using the stated probability model, then compare expected and realized outcomes. Seeded draws reproduce the same experiment.
Simulation.Objective: Compare the consequences of your decisions with the weighted scoring targets.
Simulation.Theory: Expected value is the probability-weighted payoff, not a promise about one realized outcome. Compare risky choices with a guaranteed alternative.
Simulation.Strategy: Calculate the expected outcome before deciding. Use the probability model to justify protection against unfavorable outcomes.

Events.Name: Stable experiment
Events.Description: Model parameters stay fixed; a new seeded sample is drawn.

Simulation.Strategy: Calculate the expected outcome before deciding. Use the probability model to justify protection against unfavorable outcomes.

Simulation.Name: Net Present Value Decision Lab

Simulation.Strategy: Approve positive-NPV capital only when the cash buffer can cover the payment delay. Compare IRR with the cost of capital.

Simulation.Name: Dividend versus Reinvestment Decision Lab
Simulation.Briefing: Dividend versus Reinvestment: invest now for four future period cash flows. Yield per period: 38,7% of capital; discount rate: funding rate plus 4 percentage points. New capital earns from the next round.
Simulation.Objective: Compare the consequences of your decisions with the weighted scoring targets.
Simulation.Theory: NPV discounts future cash flows; IRR is the rate where NPV is zero. Borrowing adds interest and can exhaust liquidity before returns arrive.
Simulation.Strategy: Approve positive-NPV capital only when the cash buffer can cover the payment delay. Compare IRR with the cost of capital.
